title: The Go-Go Years
theme: Shotgun. Tighten Up. Dancing In The Street. The 1960s didn't ask you to sit down — Motown, Stax, and everything in between built a decade's worth of records designed for one purpose: movement.
narrativePurpose: Test knowledge of the uptempo dance records that defined 1960s R&B — the songs built for the floor, the labels that produced them, and the artists who made standing still feel like a personal failure.
toneProgression: The dance anthems every soul fan knows → the labels, chart stories, and artists behind the uptempo side of the decade → the deeper cuts and details that separate casual listeners from true students of the era

vault.note: Digit 4 (index 3) is always visible. Vault code 1-9-6-5 — the year Four Tops' 'I Can't Help Myself' and Junior Walker's 'Shotgun' both hit #1 on the R&B charts, and James Brown's 'I Got You (I Feel Good)' became one of the most recognizable openings in soul music history. Three of the most kinetic records ever made, in the same calendar year. 1965 didn't ask you to sit down.

questions.question: Junior Walker & The All Stars' 1965 dance classic 'Shotgun' was anchored by which instrument — played by Walker himself as the lead voice of the track?

questions.question: 'Mustang Sally' — made famous by Wilson Pickett in 1966 — was written not by Pickett but by which fellow soul musician, who had recorded an earlier version of the song himself in 1965?

metadata.fact: Mack Rice — known as 'Bonny' Rice — wrote 'Mustang Sally' and released it on Blue Rock Records in May 1965. Wilson Pickett's 1966 Atlantic recording became the definitive version.
metadata.storyHook: Pickett made it famous. Mack Rice wrote it. The credit follows the hit, not the writer.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Mustang Sally' was written and first recorded by Mack Rice, released on Blue Rock label in May 1965. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mustang_Sally_(song)

sources.title: Mustang Sally (song) – Wikipedia

metadata.fact: David Porter has described in interviews how Hayes was in the bathroom and called out the phrase when Porter was rushing him. The phrase became the song's title.
metadata.storyHook: The greatest soul anthem of 1966 started with a bathroom break and an impatient writing partner.

questions.question: 'I Can't Help Myself (Sugar Pie Honey Bunch)' — Four Tops' 1965 #1 — was written and produced by which Motown songwriting and production trio, whose initials became one of the most celebrated bylines in soul music history?

metadata.song: I Can't Help Myself (Sugar Pie Honey Bunch)
metadata.fact: Holland-Dozier-Holland — Brian Holland, Lamont Dozier, and Eddie Holland — wrote and produced dozens of Motown's defining hits in the 1960s, including 'Reach Out I'll Be There,' 'Stop! In the Name of Love,' and 'Baby I Need Your Loving.'
metadata.storyHook: Three names. One hyphen. The most productive songwriting team in Motown history.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'I Can't Help Myself (Sugar Pie Honey Bunch)' is written and produced by Holland-Dozier-Holland (Brian Holland, Lamont Dozier, Eddie Holland). After leaving Motown in 1968, HDH founded Hot Wax Records and Invictus Records.

questions.question: 'Shotgun' was co-produced by Harvey Fuqua — a Motown executive who, before his production career, was the lead vocalist of which celebrated 1950s doo-wop group?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 3 OF 3 — SHOTGUN PRODUCER'S DOO-WOP ROOTS

metadata.artist: Junior Walker & The All Stars / Harvey Fuqua
metadata.fact: Harvey Fuqua was the lead singer of The Moonglows, one of the defining doo-wop acts of the 1950s. He later joined Motown as a producer and A&R figure, co-producing Junior Walker's earliest recordings.
metadata.storyHook: Before Harvey Fuqua was making records at Motown, he was singing doo-wop with The Moonglows. The producer behind 'Shotgun' had a whole career before the career.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Harvey Fuqua was the former lead singer of The Moonglows and later joined Motown as a producer and A&R figure, co-producing Junior Walker's earliest recordings including 'Shotgun.'

reserve.question: 'Goin' to a Go-Go' referenced the go-go club culture that swept American cities in the mid-1960s. Which Sunset Strip venue — opened in 1964 — is widely credited with popularizing go-go dancing in America?

metadata.fact: The Whisky a Go Go opened on the Sunset Strip in Los Angeles in January 1964 and introduced go-go dancers — performing on elevated platforms — to American audiences.
metadata.storyHook: Los Angeles had the venue. Detroit had the record. Together they named an era.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: The Whisky a Go Go opened on the Sunset Strip in Los Angeles in January 1964 and is widely credited with popularizing go-go dancing in America.

metadata.storyHook: The writers who built Motown's sound left and started their own label. The hits kept coming.
